title: Writing for Red's group and the move to a big band
summary: He writes most of the group's book, plays the Hickory House and 52nd Street, then goes west; gives up trumpet and meets his wife.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: But you did most of the writing them for Red's group, then?
They were playing at the Hickory House for a while?

Then they wandered around 52nd Street and then he wanted to do a bigger band and we went up to Syracuse, I think, and then we went to the west coast after that. I think it was (inaudible), in Los Angeles.

I played trumpet until that summer of '37 and then gave it up. I met my wife at this period, she came from northern Wisconsin. I went up there for a mastoid operation and she was a nurse in those days,
she helped take care of me. That's how I met her.
We're looking at a copy of the New Yorker with a picture of a distinguished three story house and there's a sign in front that says, The Smythes. Since 1937, an old fashioned marriage.
